system.name: Homans' Social Exchange Theory (studied with LLM-based agents)
system.one_liner: Studies and extends Homans' Social Exchange Theory with a virtual society of three LLM agents playing a resource exchange game.

content.variant_note: six equal cards in a 2 by 3 grid, each a pastel title band over a cartoon vignette of two agents trading, with bubbles, bars or a table
content.argues: Homans' theory is made of six propositions, each of which can be seen as a small scene of agents exchanging resources.
content.subject: Six propositions of Homans' Social Exchange Theory, each shown as a toy exchange scene between cartoon agents.

elements.name: (a) Success Proposition
elements.role: successful exchanges make an agent want to exchange with the same partner again
elements.drawn_as: card with a blue title band: rising blue bars over Round 1, Round 2 and Round N, a red dashed rising arrow to a gift box, two agents with bubbles below

elements.name: (b) Stimulus Proposition
elements.role: agents seek partners who provided help before when they need a resource
elements.drawn_as: card with a yellow title band: a thought cloud where one agent hands Resource B to another (Providing Help), an agent below saying she is short on B

elements.name: (c) Value Proposition
elements.role: combinations of different resources are worth more than a single resource
elements.drawn_as: card with a green title band: circles A = 1, A + B = 4, A + B + C = 9, a Resource Pool of A, B and C, an agent saying better together

elements.name: (d) Deprivation–Satiation Proposition
elements.role: an agent with an excess of one resource looks for the ones it lacks
elements.drawn_as: card with an orange title band: two small bar charts (Deprivation, Satiation) each with a B token and an emoji, a dashed Accumulating Resource box, an agent saying too much B

elements.name: (e) Aggression–Approval Proposition
elements.role: under- and over-delivery in an exchange provoke different emotional responses
elements.drawn_as: card with a pink title band, titled Resource Exchange: two rows of bubble and emoji separated by a dashed line, angry face above, warm face below

elements.name: (f) Rationality Proposition
elements.role: agents weigh profit against reliability when choosing a trading partner
elements.drawn_as: card with a grey title band: one agent facing two candidate agents in a dashed box, a Profit and Safety table with ticks and a cross, a thumbs-up, caption Action Value X Success Probability

elements.name: Resource tokens A, B, C
elements.drawn_as: circles with a letter: A orange, B blue, C green

elements.name: Experience / Future Requirements
elements.role: past exchanges shape what an agent will need and ask for next
elements.drawn_as: two bold labels at the right of the thought cloud

elements.name: Profit / Safety table
elements.role: compares two candidate partners on the two criteria
elements.drawn_as: 2 by 2 grid with blue header cells, a small avatar per row, green ticks and one red cross

lessons.what_to_learn: Present a set of parallel concepts as equal framed cards, each with a pastel title band and a toy scene played by the same recurring characters, with one short speech bubble stating the idea, so a theory reads as six small stories.
lessons.suits: Explaining a set of named propositions, principles or behaviours with one toy scenario each, when every idea fits one frame with two actors.

evidence: Illustration and examples of the six propositions in Homans’ Social Exchange Theory.
people may balance potential profits against transaction reliability when selecting trading partners (Figure 1(f)).

summary: The paper studies Homans' Social Exchange Theory with LLM-based agents. Figure 1, in the preliminaries, introduces the theory's six propositions as a 2 by 3 grid of equal cards, each headed by a pastel title band: Success, Stimulus, Value, Deprivation-Satiation, Aggression-Approval and Rationality. Each card is a cartoon vignette in which recurring characters trade resources A, B and C: rising bars over rounds with a gift at the end, a thought cloud of past help, circles that add up to 1, 4 and 9, bars of holdings with emoji reactions, angry versus warm replies to broken or extra deliveries, and a profit and safety table with ticks and a cross. Short speech bubbles paraphrase each idea.
summary_zh: 论文用大模型智能体研究霍曼斯社会交换理论。图在预备知识中用 2×3 等大卡片介绍六条命题：成功、刺激、价值、剥夺—满足、攻击—赞同、理性；每张卡有彩色标题条和卡通人物交换资源 A、B、C 的小场景，配对话气泡、柱状图、表情和打勾表。
notes: The prior pass listed contribution-mosaic first; the cards illustrate the theory under study (Preliminary section), not the paper's own contributions, so scope-overview leads. The character art may be AI-generated; its origin cannot be told. The preview may substitute the sans font named in the SVG (Microsoft YaHei).
